payload.rationale:
I estimate a 3% chance of YES. The threshold requires at least four distinct Atlantic hurricanes reaching Category 3 or higher within the contract window. The supplied NHC summary reports zero hurricanes and zero major hurricanes through September 18 at 21 UTC, so four major hurricanes would still need to occur, absent retrospective revisions. The reported five named storms and ACE of 4.4 also indicate an unusually quiet season to date.

The supplied climatological average of three major hurricanes is for an entire season, not the remaining period. General seasonal background places September 19 after the usual activity peak, although late September and October can still produce powerful hurricanes. Four remaining majors would therefore be an exceptional late-season concentration. My judgment also treats the extremely quiet first portion of the season as some evidence of persistent unfavorable conditions, not merely elapsed time.

The estimate could be too high if those unfavorable conditions persist, leaving very few opportunities for major-hurricane development. It could be too low if the quiet season reflects temporary suppression and conditions shift sharply: major hurricanes can cluster, making a simple average-rate model understate the upper tail.
limitations: The supplied current-season figures are saved search-index excerpts; full NHC pages were not independently verified.
No current basin forecast, environmental diagnostics, or fitted conditional late-season model is supplied.
The inference that early-season inactivity predicts reduced later activity is a transfer assumption, not an observed environmental diagnosis.
Observations after September 18 at 21 UTC and retrospective NHC classification revisions are not included.
